title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of St George Mining Limited. Must obtain prior written approval of the Chairman (or the Board, if the Chairman is the one trading) before buying, selling or exercising rights in Company securities.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the Company's activities; determined by the Company to be its Directors and the direct reports of the Managing Director. Non-director KMP must obtain prior written approval of the Managing Director before buying, selling or exercising rights in Company securities.

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's Annual Financial Report
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the Company's Annual Financial Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Consolidated Interim Financial Report
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the Consolidated Interim Financial Report

windows.start_anchor: two weeks prior to the release of the Company's quarterly reports
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release of the Company's quarterly reports

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may at its discretion vary (including relax) the Block Out Period rule for a particular Block Out Period by general announcement to all Directors or KMP, before or during that period; the Policy does not provide for the Company to declare additional ad hoc blackout periods beyond the three stated Block Out Periods, and does not address confidentiality of any variation. A person in possession of price sensitive information must not deal at any time regardless.

rules.detail: No definition of 'Dealing' or 'Securities' addressing derivatives. The policy only covers 'securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue'; options are mentioned only as Company-issued options under an employee/director option scheme, not third-party OTC derivatives over Company shares.
No hedging provision of any kind anywhere in the Policy.
Short selling is not named anywhere; only short-term trading (a distinct concept, clause 4.2) is addressed.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere.

Not itself restricted or requiring approval. The clause 5 approval regime covers only a Director or KMP who wishes to 'buy, sell or exercise rights' in Company securities, which does not naturally extend to entering a lending arrangement; a secured lender's own disposal of the shares on default is expressly treated as a permitted exception from the Block Out Period ban.
rules.evidence: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Granting security over Company securities by way of mortgage or charge is not named as a dealing requiring approval. The policy addresses only the insider-trading risk of a lender-forced sale and confirms that a sale under a mortgage or charge as a consequence of default does not itself breach insider trading laws.
rules.evidence: Where Company securities are provided to a lender as security by way of mortgage or charge, a sale that occurs under that mortgage or charge as a consequence of default would not breach insider trading laws.

rules.detail: No general secured-financing prohibition or disclosure obligation. Only a 'secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement' is contemplated, and only in the context of exempting the resulting forced sale from the Block Out Period ban.
rules.evidence: dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

rules.detail: Ban on short-term trading, with a carve-out for selling shares shortly after exercising options, which remains subject to the Block Out Period rules. No specific holding period is defined.
rules.evidence: Directors or Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

clearance.approver: Chairman (or, if the Chairman wishes to trade, the Board)
clearance.evidence: Any Director wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Chairman or the Board before doing so.
Any Key Management Personnel wishing to buy, sell or exercise rights in relation to the Company's securities must obtain the prior written approval of the Managing Director before doing so.

clearance.approver: Managing Director (for KMP); Chairman (for a Director); all other Board members (for the Chairman)
clearance.evidence: Directors or Key Management Personnel who are not in possession of inside information in relation to the Company, may be given prior written clearance ... to sell or otherwise dispose of Company securities in a Block-Out Period where the person is in severe financial hardship or where there are exceptional circumstances ... Any exemption, if issued, will be in writing and shall contain a specified time period during which the sale of securities can be made.

carve_outs: exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter (still subject to Block Out Period restrictions)
short_term.evidence: Directors or Key Management Personnel should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities except for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

exceptions.evidence: acquire Company securities under a dividend reinvestment, or top-up plan that is available to all holders or securities of the same class
acquire, or agree to acquire or exercise options under a Company Share Option Plan
transfer securities of the Company already held into a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the restricted person is a beneficiary

make an investment in, or trade in units of, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme only investing in the securities of the Company) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
undertake to accept, or accept, a takeover offer
dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

exercise (but not sell securities following exercise) an option or a right under an employee incentive scheme ... where the final date for the exercise ... falls during a prohibited period ... and the restricted person could not reasonably have been expected to exercise it at a time when free to do so
trade under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this Policy

exemption_authority: Managing Director (for KMP), Chairman (for a Director), or all other Board members (for the Chairman) may grant a written, time-limited exemption from the Block Out Period ban for severe financial hardship (a pressing financial commitment satisfiable only by selling) or exceptional circumstances (court order, court-enforceable undertaking, or other overriding legal/regulatory requirement), on a written application with supporting documentation; independent verification from banks or accountants may be sought.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy applies to both the sale and purchase of any securities of the Company and its subsidiaries on issue from time to time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike sibling template policies (e.g. Kentor Gold's hedging ban), this Policy has no hedging or derivatives clause at all, and the approval regime is framed only around a person who wishes to 'buy, sell or exercise rights' in Company securities, so it is genuinely unclear whether entering an OTC put/call with a bank is caught by the Policy at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors or Key Management Personnel may at any time: ... dispose of securities of the Company resulting from a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an express, broadly worded exception (not limited to margin loans) from the Block Out Period restrictions, giving a bank real ability to enforce its security over the collared shares even during a closed period.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Were this to occur at a time when the person possessed inside information, then the sale of Company securities would be a breach of insider trading laws, even though the person's decision to sell was not influenced by the inside information that the person possessed and the person may not have made a profit on the sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A margin call or lender demand under the collar's loan that forces a sale while the executive holds inside information would still breach insider trading law regardless of intent, so the facility needs standstill or cure provisions to avoid forced sales during blackout or UPSI periods.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the management of the sale of any significant volume of Company securities (i.e. a volume that would represent a volume in excess of 10% of the total securities held by the seller prior to the sale, or a volume to be sold that would be in excess of 10% of the average daily traded volume ... for the preceding 20 trading days) ... needs to be discussed with the board and the Company's legal advisers prior to the execution of any sale.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unwinding or hedge-related sales that exceed 10% of the executive's holding or 10% of 20-day ADV trigger a mandatory board and legal-adviser discussion, documented in a file note, before the bank can execute that leg of the collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any Directors or Key Management Personnel who (or through his or her Associates) buys, sells, or exercises rights in relation to Company securities must notify the Company Secretary in writing of the details of the transaction within five (5) business days of the transaction occurring.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or its collateral through a family trust or other Associate does not avoid the post-trade notification obligation, which must be met within 5 business days regardless of who executes the trade.

bespoke_clauses.topic: policy does not override the law
bespoke_clauses.clause: Compliance with these guidelines for trading in the Company's securities does not absolve that individual from complying with the law, which must be the overriding consideration when trading in the Company's securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because the Policy is largely silent on derivatives, hedging and secured financing, compliance with its express terms provides limited comfort; independent insider trading and market misconduct analysis is still required for the collar and loan.

summary: A funded collar over vested St George Mining shares is not expressly addressed by this Policy at all: there is no hedging or derivatives clause, and the approval regime in clause 5 is framed only around a person who wishes to 'buy, sell or exercise rights' in Company securities, leaving genuine doubt whether entering an OTC put and call with a bank falls within its scope. If it does, Directors need prior written approval from the Chairman (or Board) and KMP from the Managing Director, outside the two-week pre-results Block Out Periods and absent price sensitive information, with post-trade notification to the Company Secretary within 5 business days. The loan leg is comparatively well supported: margin lending and other secured financing arrangements are not prohibited, and a secured lender's enforcement sale on default is expressly exempted from the Block Out Period ban, though a margin call forcing a sale while the executive holds inside information would still breach insider trading law. Any leg of the structure exceeding 10% of the executive's holding or 10% of 20-day average daily volume triggers mandatory board and legal-adviser sign-off before execution. Given the silence on hedging, this Policy should not be relied upon alone; independent advice on whether the collar constitutes insider trading or market misconduct is essential before proceeding.
